claims.assessment: Reuses row-local normalization; 34 full NS certificates, all eleven coefficient fields, 64 local states, and missing-query controls; no new multirow coverage

claims.summary: Over the base A, B, E=P(1+A,1+B), fresh helpers lose zero degrees at rank two (any count, third-level base too), one at rank three, two at rank four; the rank-three gain is realized by a verified witness with s-free helper cofactors, exactly the sufficient gain criterion
claims.assessment: Exact finite refutation of an additive-constant, rank-independent loss; sequential total-rank bound D+sum k_a delta_a is the proved ceiling; two rank-three helpers and rank five untested

claims.summary: At accuracy one over F2, t is a degree-D consequence of a fresh block iff there are Q^alpha in the input ideal with cofactor degree <= D-e_i-|alpha| such that t+Q^empty and every coefficient polynomial (1+sum_{j in alpha} g_j)Q^alpha+sum_j g_j Q^{alpha minus j} lie in the base space through D-|alpha|
claims.assessment: Working exact reformulation of the NS identity by fresh-coefficient monomials; specialization and the gain criterion are its special cases

claims.summary: An accuracy-one block on two affine inputs never adds degree-D consequences in the existing variables, over any base with Boolean equations
claims.assessment: Rediscovery of the top-level case of `lem:rank-two-bottom-quadratic-transfer` (substitution r=(1,1+g_1)); second proof from the coefficient criterion; rank three fails by `ex:rank-dependent-fresh-block-loss`

claims.summary: Over F2, a fresh accuracy-one block with affine inputs adds no degree-D consequence in the existing variables when the base is Boolean equations plus complete accuracy-one affine blocks, at any rank
claims.assessment: Conjecture with about twenty exact checks (ranks three and four, coefficient-mixed, overlapping, cyclic inputs); losses so far need a second-level base block; no substitution or degree-exactness proof possible; an instance on the functional PHP base with dense inputs (eight holes, degree four, ranks three and four) is conservative, see `check:augmented-php-degree-small-boards` (2026-09-18)

claims.summary: The one-level theorem dualizes to a weighted-substitution design; the fresh-block losses are finite instances of second-level inputs that are sums of low flat indicators, the recorded composition frontier
claims.assessment: Review turn; high-only readings would compose additively but exclude all low blocks, so no new route

claims.assessment: Decision from proof reading; restricted extension for high-only readings sketched with ledger B'=n^(3/4) polylog, not proved

claims.summary: Matching restriction cannot make dense low-rank forms constant on any polynomial residual, and (claim corrected in `cor:polylog-high-threshold-cube-volume`) enlarging the weight degree was said not to lower the high threshold; the open zone is a level-two block of small affine rank reading many distinct low blocks, or a middle-rank block reading any low block
claims.assessment: Decision from proof reading; states once where weight clamping, profile induction, and literal restriction all stop

claims.summary: The restriction of multilinear polynomials of degree <= k to a flat of codimension r has dimension <= sum_{j<=k} C(v-r,j) <= 2 e^{-rk/v} C(v,k) for k <= (v-r)/3
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof; replaces the crude C(v-r+k,k) estimate whose threshold r >= k + v ln(8M)/k is never below 2 sqrt(v ln 8M)

claims.summary: In the cube-volume framework with k = floor((n/4-D)/(2D+1)) and D >= max(13, ell), affine tuples of rank >= v ln(16M)/k = O(D ell log M) are clamped by the weight and all others are packed by one-bin telescoping; the survivors on the weight's support are narrow terms
claims.assessment: Working parameter corollary of the recorded finite theorem; corrects the rebalancing claim of `obs:middle-rank-frontier`

claims.summary: Over qn+1 points, an r-disjunction restricted by a random partial q-matching leaving q ell+1 points has canonical matching decision tree of height >= s with probability < (4 e^q r^{1/q} p^q n^{q-1/q})^s, for 6 <= ell = pn <= (n/r)^{1/q^2}/e
claims.assessment: Imported statement, Beame, A Switching Lemma Primer (1994), Section 5, Lemma 4, read with its proof from an open copy; bipartite PHP-board versions (PBI 1993, KPW 1995) cited, unavailable locally

claims.summary: A matching decision tree of height s that represents and refines a disjunction of terms of size <= r yields a complete old-only image of the ENS block reading those terms: product and coefficient images of degree <= s, companions through r+s, coefficient identity through s, Booleanity through 2s, over point axioms, exclusions, and Boolean equations
claims.assessment: Working proof using only representation, refinement, and the old axioms; holds verbatim for bipartite trees on the PHP board

claims.summary: With ell ~ n^{1/4} r^{-1/4} and s = ceil(log2(2M)), a common restriction gives all M readers of width-r literal terms images with certificates through r + 2 log2(2M), on a residual of Theta(n^{1/4} r^{-1/4}) points
claims.assessment: Parameter corollary in the nonbipartite setting; bipartite constants unverified; readers with a parity input not covered

claims.summary: On the (n+1) x n board, for an r-disjunction and 1 <= s <= ell <= n-1, the fraction of size-(n-ell) partial matchings whose canonical matching decision tree has height >= s is at most (ell+1)^s sum_{j>=s/2} A^j <= 2((ell+1) sqrt(A))^s, A = 4 r ell (ell+1)/((n-ell+1) ln 2) <= 1/2
claims.assessment: Working proof adapted from Beame's q-matching argument with an explicit encoding (code, masks, partner indices in known vertex sets); encoding verified by exact round trips on small boards; constants generous

claims.summary: A conjunction of r bit literals on rho rows decodes, modulo I_r(F^fun), to the sum of the at most n^rho pairwise incompatible unary terms assigning each row a consistent hole
claims.assessment: Working proof by row-wise expansion with functional exclusions

claims.summary: With inputs that are sums of pairwise incompatible unary terms and a representing, refining tree of height s, full leaf terms as coefficient images give companions and the coefficient identity through r+s and Booleanity through 2s
claims.assessment: Working extension of `lem:switched-reader-old-image`; cross terms vanish by row conflicts

claims.summary: The switching lemma's extension count needs uniform partial matchings, while the weight step needs the compact subcube family with a fixed residual subcube; in that family extensions give ratio C(N,j)(N+1)_j >= 1, and after a uniform restriction the residual is not affine; unary weight fails by ambient dimension mn
claims.assessment: Decision from reading; sharpened by `lem:subcube-bit-switching` (light rows switch in the family) and `ex:fixed-subcube-pinned-rows-refuted` (pinned rows do not); the width-one subcube case is the recorded positive-literal swap count

claims.summary: In the slack subcube family Phi_e (N+1+e residual pigeons, e free outside labels, fixed residual subcube of size N), a reader with <= r rows per term and <= w literals per row, w <= l-l_2-1, e >= 2^{w+2} s, has canonical-tree height >= s with probability <= A^s + M r exp(-e 2^{-w-4}), A = 2r(N+e)e(N+e+1)/(n-N-e+1); the tree transfers to the compact family Phi_0; with e=N, N^3 <= n/(48r), w <= log2 N - log2 s - 6, s = ceil(log2(8M)) one restriction serves all readers
claims.assessment: Working proof by an extension encoding whose code stays in Phi_{e-s}; encoding verified by 76,418 exact round trips at n in {8,16}; composes with `lem:bit-term-decoder-image`, `lem:sum-input-switched-image`, and the weight step for rows of at most about (1/3) log2 n literals

claims.summary: For the fixed subcube Q, the reader OR_i [row i pinned to q_{i mod N}] (n+1 one-row terms of l literals, rank l <= r_high) has, for all but an N^{-1/10} fraction of Phi_0, no matching decision tree of height below N/(2 log2 N + 35) whose leaves falsify every term or contain a satisfied term
claims.assessment: Refutation by an adversary argument, all sizes; concerns syntactic representation, not representation modulo the residual ideal

claims.summary: An extension encoding in any family whose residual holes form a flat gains only from the residual pigeons and can record a residual row only by matching it to a consistent free label outside the flat, so it covers exactly rows with at most about log2(e/s) literals; a uniformly random flat defeats the pinned-row reader and keeps the lemma, leaving row widths between (1/3) log2 n and (c-1/3) log2 n open for M = n^c
claims.assessment: Obstruction with a proposed family; the affine invariance of the weight step under a random flat is not verified

claims.summary: Restricting to a uniformly random affine flat Q of dimension l_2 (live rows uniform, others matched bijectively outside Q) maps degree-d old-bit polynomials to degree <= d in the residual bits, maps Q_n into the ideal of Q_N with certificates through l, and keeps the affine decoder consistent modulo the residual row axiom; the multiplier space, flat count, and cube detector apply verbatim on Q
claims.assessment: Working proof; the recorded coordinate restriction is the special case of a coordinate subcube

claims.summary: In the random-flat family, a reader whose light part (rows below w_0 literals) satisfies the subcube switching hypotheses has, with probability >= 1 - A^s - M r exp(-e 2^{-w-4}) - M_h r (N+1+e)(N+2r) 2^{-w_0}/n, a tree of height < s whose 1-leaves contain a satisfied term and whose 0-leaves falsify every light term while heavy terms are falsified or vanish modulo residual Booleanity; hence complete switching for sources of size S <= n/(768 s r (N+2r)); refined on 2026-09-18 (`entry-2026-09-18-literal-window`) to (N+1) in place of (N+1+e), giving completeness up to n^{4/3}/polylog and a window from (1/3) log2 n to (c-1) log2 n for S = n^c, c > 4/3
claims.assessment: Working proof (heavy-term dichotomy, no change to the canonical tree; light lemma round-trip tested on random flats with 54,713 exact round trips); the window is the remaining literal-frontier gap

claims.summary: Making the canonical tree skip terms with a row that has no consistent unused hole of Q breaks the extension encoding: a moved row's consistent outside code label can revive a skipped term for the decoder
claims.assessment: Refutation by round-trip failures (114 to 1,206 per run) with the mechanism read off a failing case; does not apply to the wide-round tree, whose skip tests only unplaced wide rows (`lem:wide-annihilation`, 2026-09-18)

claims.summary: A hole-query node with branches X_{jq} over uncovered pigeons and the empty branch u_q = 1 - sum_j X_{jq} has branch factors summing to one identically, pairwise products zero modulo Boolean and exclusion axioms at degree two, and idempotent u_q; trees with such nodes keep leaf degree <= height, the leaf partition identity, and pairwise incompatibility, so the switched-reader image lemmas extend verbatim without any onto axiom
claims.assessment: Working proof

claims.summary: The light range (1/3) log2 n is intrinsic to extension encodings in flat families (the free-set entropy is the gain; a fixed free pool only raises the family ratio); a window term is alive-unsatisfied with a Q-consistent heavy row with probability <= r 4^r (N+1)N/n times the product of its pattern densities, against >= 2^{-2r-1} times the product for satisfaction, so the window matters only for readers with correlated satisfaction events; the sufficient obligation is a bound on >= k_0 alive window terms with distinct heavy rows and no satisfied term (corrected on 2026-09-18 by `ex:random-flat-pigeon-only-refuted`: the holes must also be distinct, and the tree must use hole queries)
claims.assessment: Observation with the refuted fixed-pool variant and a named sufficient obligation; scope narrowed 2026-09-18: the (1/3) log2 n limit holds for encodings that move any residual row of the slack tree in Phi_e (the residual factor N+e+1), while the pair-space encoding of the restricted tree moves rows of R' only, keeps the free-set entropy, and admits e up to n^(2-eps-c)/4400 (`lem:pair-space-decoder`, [correction of scope](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#pair-space-encoding)); the fixed-pool refutation stands; `obs:shared-wide-cube` (2026-09-18) shows hole queries necessary per reader already at size n for one wide pattern shared by n/2 rows

claims.summary: In the random-flat family the single-target reader F_{x*} = OR_i [row i pinned to x*] is, with probability N/n (the event x* in Q), unsatisfied and without any pigeon-only deciding tree of height < N-1, while one hole query at x* decides it; the n readers F_{x*} (size n^2) contain a bad one for every restriction
claims.assessment: Refutation, working proof; corrects the window obligation to distinct holes; corrected again on 2026-09-18 (`obs:alive-pair-matching-obligation`) to a matching bound, with the rank effect (N/n)^{rank} for prescribed labels in a random flat

claims.summary: For unary heavy rows the alive pinned pairs (residual row, label in Q) form a bipartite graph B; a tree decides the pinned part in height equal to the vertex cover number = matching number nu(B) (König), and no tree does better when no term is satisfied; the readers OR_x [i_0 -> x] and F_{x*} show that distinct holes alone or distinct rows alone do not suffice; dense pinned classes (>= n ln(8SK) pairs) are satisfied by matched edges when their tail is (negative association of a uniform bijection, imported from Joag-Dev and Proschan 1983), sparse classes have few alive pairs in expectation; the missing step is an exponential tail for nu(B) over the random flat
claims.assessment: Observation and reduction principle with an imported lemma; the general bound is open

claims.summary: Given (Q, R'), if at least Delta_0 = N + 2(n-N) ln(8S)/D* labels have degree >= D* >= 2(N+1) in a unary reader, some term is satisfied by the uniform bijection mu' with probability >= 1 - 1/(8S)
claims.assessment: Working proof from negative association of a uniform bijection (Joag-Dev and Proschan 1983, imported)

claims.summary: Alive pinned pairs with labels of degree < D* = k_1(n-k_1)/(2e(N+1)N) have matching number >= k_1 with probability <= 2^{-k_1}, by the symmetric sum of degrees over the flat's N points and the uniform residual set
claims.assessment: Working proof; uses only |Q| = N, no affine structure; bounds the heavy rounds of the both-endpoints tree directly ([transfer](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#both-endpoints-rule))

claims.summary: A set D of labels meets a uniformly random flat of size N in >= k_2 points with probability <= |D|^{k_2} (N/n)^{ceil(log2 k_2)+1}
claims.assessment: Working proof by affine rank and transitivity

claims.summary: In the random-flat family a unary reader has, with probability >= 1 - 1/(8S) - Delta_0^{k_2}(N/n)^{ceil(log2 k_2)+1} - 2^{-k_1}, a pigeon-and-hole-query tree of height <= k_1 + k_2 whose 1-leaves contain a satisfied term and whose 0-leaves falsify or annihilate every term; for S = n^c readers, k_1 = ceil(log2(16S)), k_2 = 2^{c+2}, one restriction serves all unary readers with height O(log S + 2^c); readers with separate light and unary terms are covered with the light encoding
claims.assessment: Working proof; first literal-frontier result without a size regime; mixed terms (pinned row with light tail) open; corrected 2026-09-18: the separate-terms corollary must run the light part first, since a pinned row that is light elsewhere is invisible to the decoder ([two-role rows](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#two-role-rows))

claims.summary: In the canonical tree for mixed readers, querying the pigeon when its row has at least two unkilled pairs of B_0 (residual row, label in Q, tails ignored) and otherwise the hole makes every path's heavy queries pairwise distinct in rows and holes, hence at most nu(B_t) with B_t the pairs whose tail is not falsified; the decoder recomputes the rule from the code, so the light encoding applies with heavy queries recorded unmoved
claims.assessment: Working proof; the probabilistic bound on nu(B_t) for mixed readers is decomposed into satisfied, alive-matched, and alive-unmatched classes and left open; part (ii) corrected 2026-09-18: a light query at a row pinned in an earlier heavy round is recorded, not moved, costing one factor N+e per heavy query ([recording rule](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#two-role-rows)); corrected again 2026-09-18: the recording rule may cost every light query for two-role rows, so part (ii) holds for role-separated readers ([correction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#two-role-gap)); part (i) refuted 2026-09-18: pigeon queries can repeat a trigger hole, so the distinct-holes and nu(B_t) claims fail; replaced by the hole-only rule ([counterexample and correction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#adaptive-rule-gap)); the conclusion of part (i) holds for the both-endpoints rule ([rule](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#both-endpoints-rule))

claims.summary: Preferring, among non-falsified terms, the earliest whose pinned pair is matched makes every heavy query come from a class with no matched pinned pair, so the heavy queries of a path number at most nu(B_um), the matching number of alive pairs of unmatched classes with non-falsified tails; decoder-computable
claims.assessment: Working proof; the reader OR_x OR_i [i -> x] and [j in p_x] is shown not to be a counterexample because classes with labels outside Q are matched by the occupants, leaving a rank bound for survivor sets as the last step; corrected 2026-09-18: on the hole-only tree the bound is the hole count of those pairs, not the matching number ([correction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#hole-only-rule)); restored as stated on the both-endpoints tree ([transfer](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#both-endpoints-rule))

claims.summary: The residual weight step needs image degrees 2s+r <= N/4, so tree height N/8-r suffices for the window and N is a free polylogarithmic parameter; heavy queries number at most 2N+1 on any path, so every literal reader switches at every polynomial size with height 6N+3c, and the open mixed-term obligation is a constant-factor bound (at most N/24 heavy queries on paths with few light answers)
claims.assessment: Working observation; enumerating light answers cannot prove the constant-factor bound (union n^(k+c) against rank gain (N^2/n)^(log k)); corrected 2026-09-18 ([two-role correction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#two-role-gap): switching conclusion for role-separated readers; the heavy bound stands); on the hole-only tree the trivial count is N ([correction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#hole-only-rule)); on the both-endpoints tree: N rounds trivially, obligation fewer than N/48 rounds ([transfer](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#both-endpoints-rule)); the two-role restriction is lifted for sparsely pinned readers by `lem:two-role-decoder` on the complete-term tree (2026-09-18); the composition sketch and the trivial O(N) height for mixed readers are unproved on the slack family (`obs:composition-gap`, 2026-09-18)

claims.summary: For any pair set P in the random-flat family, Pr[some pair alive and none matched] <= 45(N+1)^2 ln(n)/n * Pr[some pair matched]; no structure of P or of the flat is used
claims.assessment: Working proof (inclusion-exclusion lower bound, negative association upper bound, heavy rows and labels); sharp up to the logarithm

claims.summary: A light tail on at most r-1 rows is alive but not satisfied by the restriction with probability at most 2(r-1)2^w(N+1)/n times the probability that it is satisfied, also conditionally on the other rows and the flat
claims.assessment: Working proof; with the light range this factor is at most rN n^(-2/3)

claims.summary: For any mixed reader, the expected number of classes eligible to trigger a heavy query is at most theta'(1+eps_w) times the expected number of classes with a satisfied term, theta' = 45(N+1)^2 ln(n)/n (1+o(1))
claims.assessment: Working corollary in expectation; the bad-event bound needs a correlation argument by rows, since exposing all tail rows determines the flat

claims.summary: Mixed readers whose classes are full (all rows pinned to one label) with single-row light tails on pairwise distinct rows have, at every polynomial source size n^c, at most 2^(2c+2) heavy queries on every path except with probability n^(-c-1)+n^(-2c-2): many labels force a satisfied term by negative association over distinct rows, few labels bound the trigger holes by the affine rank of the label set in the flat
claims.assessment: Working theorem with full proof (random-flat family, hole-query trees); shared tail rows and non-full pair sets excluded and their required mechanisms named; corrected 2026-09-18 ([two-role correction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#two-role-gap): switching conclusion for role-separated readers; the heavy bound stands); holds on the hole-only tree, whose trigger holes are distinct; false for the adaptive tree when c >= 2 ([correction 2026-09-18](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#adaptive-rule-gap)); on the both-endpoints tree the count bounds heavy rounds, with twice as many queries ([transfer](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#both-endpoints-rule)); unary readers are contained in `thm:single-row-wide-readers` on the wide-round tree (2026-09-18)

claims.summary: Single-row full-class readers on arbitrary rows with loading Lambda(F) = sum over rows of the fraction of labels consistent with a class at most lambda_0 have fewer than (2c+2+max(4e lambda_0,(c+1)log n))2^(c+3) heavy queries on every path except with probability 3n^(-c-1): few hosting rows are residual, few matched rows are loaded (negative association), and each assigned row's survivor set in the flat is bounded by affine rank
claims.assessment: Working theorem with full proof; needs no satisfied term; does not imply the distinct-rows theorem; corrected 2026-09-18 ([two-role correction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#two-role-gap): switching conclusion for role-separated readers; the heavy bound stands); holds on the hole-only tree, whose trigger holes are distinct; false for the adaptive tree when c >= 2 ([correction 2026-09-18](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#adaptive-rule-gap)); on the both-endpoints tree the count bounds heavy rounds, with twice as many queries ([transfer](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#both-endpoints-rule))

claims.summary: Given the flat, the probability that no term is satisfied is at most exp(-sum over rows of the number of labels outside the flat consistent with a class of that row whose label is outside the flat, divided by n+1)
claims.assessment: Working proof by negative association over rows; a bad reader's loading outside the flat is at most (c+1) ln n

claims.summary: For single-row full-class readers every heavy query's hole is a label of the reader inside the flat, so heavy queries number at most the size of the label set's intersection with the flat; readers with at most n^(2/3) labels have fewer than 2^(c+3) heavy queries except with probability n^(-c-1), with no hypothesis on rows or loading
claims.assessment: Working observation and corollary (affine rank); contains Case B of the distinct-rows theorem and the bounded-loading theorem for such label sets; holds on the hole-only tree, whose trigger holes are distinct; false for the adaptive tree when c >= 2 ([correction 2026-09-18](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#adaptive-rule-gap)); on the both-endpoints tree the count bounds heavy rounds, with twice as many queries ([transfer](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#both-endpoints-rule)); corrected 2026-09-18: for label sets of size n^(2/3) the corollary gives fewer than 2^(3c+4) heavy rounds, not 2^(c+3) ([rank-step correction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#rank-step-correction))

claims.summary: Every mixed reader whose classes are full (all rows pinned to one label) with a single-row light tail, on arbitrary rows, has fewer than N/24 heavy queries on every path before a 1-leaf except with probability 8n^(-c-1), for N at least 2^(c+11)(c+2)^2 ln^2 n; six exclusions organized by labels (heavy labels in the flat and few, large survivor sets outside the flat, light out-loading forces a satisfied term, the flat's light loading is small by charging light-good pairs to light labels, few matched and few residual rows yield light holes)
claims.assessment: Working theorem with full proof; settles the window obligation for this class at every polynomial size within the height budget; contains the distinct-rows, bounded-loading, and label-set results; reviewed 2026-09-18: self pairs excluded from the light loading, threshold N_0 = 2^(2c+24)(c+2) ln n, assigned rows are those assigned before the last heavy query ([review](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#entry-2026-09-18-srf-review)); corrected 2026-09-18 ([two-role correction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#two-role-gap): switching conclusion for role-separated readers; the heavy bound stands); holds on the hole-only tree, whose trigger holes are distinct; false for the adaptive tree when c >= 2 ([correction 2026-09-18](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#adaptive-rule-gap)); on the both-endpoints tree: fewer than N/48 rounds, statement unchanged ([transfer](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/#both-endpoints-rule)); switching clause conditional 2026-09-18: its composition with the light encoding is unproved (`obs:composition-gap`), the round bound stands

claims.summary: The mixed canonical tree (matched-first preference, adaptive heavy rule, hole queries) and its encoding decode correctly on every rich bad path of six exhaustively enumerated role-separated instances (n=8, N=2, 3147 paths), and a constructed reader with a row pinned in one term and light in another fails on 2610 of 4050 and 2130 of 4450 paths

claims.summary: Polynomial-calculus form of the recorded prefix-product substitution (cycle 170): r_1 = 1, r_j = prod_{i<j}(1 + L_i) sends P to prod_j(1 + L_j) and the companions to zero modulo Booleanity and row exclusions, and maps a degree-d derivation to a base derivation of degree at most d + rho - 2 (lines kept multilinear in the new variables), fixing old polynomials; rho <= 2 fully conservative (the recorded `cor:affine-rank-two-same-degree-conservativity`), rho = 3, 4 not refutable through D_0 - 2, D_0 - 3; uses only g^2 = g and Booleanity with row exclusions
claims.assessment: Working proof; restatement of a recorded substitution

claims.summary: Exact degree-d PC closures of the functional PHP over F_2 augmented by accuracy-one blocks on dense forms: on eight holes at degree four (refutation degree five) blocks with 3 inputs (uniform half-sets, affine half-spaces, two seeds), 4 inputs, and two blocks of 3 inputs do not put 1 in the closure; for the blocks with 3 and 4 inputs the old-only part of the closure has the dimension 143643 of the base closure, so every base design of degree four extends, although the substitution bound certifies this only through degree three (two for 4 inputs); six holes at degree three is conservative in all cases (weak test); controls: rho = 2 is conservative as proved, a fake non-conservative axiom raises the old-only dimension
claims.assessment: Finite check of low power (one degree of slack); an instance on the PHP base of `conj:level-one-fresh-block-conservativity`; the exact block forms have no image at s <= 2 and V_4 cap T_3 = V_3 on eight holes

claims.summary: On the functional PHP with N holes closure tests are nonvacuous only below degree N/2 + 1; pure second-level companions have degree five (the form companion of a mixed block: four) and the recorded rank-three loss sits at degree seven, which needs N >= 14 and about 1.2e11 old monomials (1.6e7 at N = 10, d = 5, where pure companions enter unmultiplied and the mixed form companion with one multiplier of degree one; 1.3e9 at N = 12, d = 6); plain elimination with generic dense blocks cannot reach the recorded loss; symmetry, the quotient by the base closure and small non-PHP unsatisfiable bases are not covered, the last being the remaining exact test
claims.assessment: Feasibility count; confirms with numbers the remark of cycle 169

claims.summary: Imported context: Impagliazzo-Mouli-Pitassi (CCC 2023) bound PC size over F_p with M extension variables of arity O(log n); over F_2 the question reduces to the degree of the augmented system by size-degree tradeoffs; Dahiya-Mahajan-Mouli (ECCC TR23-132) reach N^(1+eps(1-delta)) extension variables of arity N^(1-eps) and size N^c for an XOR-ified generalized PHP, by restrictions that shrink extension axioms plus cleanup; both restrict extension variables to depend on original variables only, and IMP identify the recursive case with AC0[p]-Frege; DMM note that constant-depth PC also simulates CP, SOS, AC0[q]-Frege and TC0-Frege, so general bounds for it are harder than the goal; the general step (dense, nested extension variables on ordinary PHP) lies beyond both
claims.assessment: Imported statements (abstracts, IMP Theorems 1 and 2 and Section 3 remark, DMM Theorem 1.2 and proof outline read; proofs not read)

claims.summary: The level-by-level collapse of wide low-rank generic readers is the recorded removal of an input span containing one, applied to the images of the inputs (cost zero; exact image 1 + sum c_i q_i whenever it annihilates every input); together with clamping and packing it leaves exactly the frontier of `obs:middle-rank-frontier` and `cor:polylog-high-threshold-cube-volume`: generic readers with term rank between about c log n / log log n and the high threshold, including the balanced rank; the induction does not close and the proposal of the previous entry is withdrawn as a route
claims.assessment: Composition of recorded results; no new lemma

claims.summary: PC form over F_2 of the recorded case split of `audit:adaptive-query-fixed-distribution-gap`: if F + {Z} and F + {1+Z} both have PC refutations of degree B for a Boolean-valued Z of degree w <= B, then F has one of degree B + w; so for any a flats some sign vector keeps F hard through D_0 - 1 - a w (additive loss, the recorded rank-control obligation)
claims.assessment: Restatement of a recorded lemma; only the PC proof and the term-value phrasing are new

claims.summary: Reduction: if PHP + {Z_c + e_c} has no degree-B refutation for some values e_c of the first-level flat indicators of rank at most w, a pure source reading only those products has none of degree B / max(1, w-1); the source must be pure (inputs are F_2-affine combinations of earlier products); extends the constant-value profiles of `lem:clamped-bottom-zero-source-profile` from weight-supplied zero clamps to arbitrary constants under a hardness hypothesis; Question H: do independent generic flats below the covering threshold a ln(1/(1-2^-w)) = v ln 2, with a margin (and v - a of order N for w = 1), leave PHP_N hard through N/8, and near and above it is there always a cheap covering certificate or a hard sign vector? Not given by weights (count), restrictions (Lemma I; constant forms on a sub-board only for about log n / log log n forms) or the case split; not a statement about literal terms
claims.assessment: Reduction proved; question open

claims.summary: Exact degree-d PC closures over F_2 with random dense axioms added one at a time, on the functional PHP (six and eight holes), the satisfiable bijective board and labelings: the first count at which 1 enters, for parity constraints and rank-two terms; closure increments are seed-independent generic ranks until one saturation jump, which on the PHP is the tipping (quotient 36 to 4953 left before it) and on the controls leads to the vanishing ideal of the surviving models at a comparable count; the PHP never tipped before the jump of the bijective control or of the labelings with affine forms, and tipped earlier (factor about 0.7 to 0.85 after normalisation) than the labelings with uniform forms; random signs survived 14 to 16 parity constraints at degree three on eight holes where the case split guarantees one; counts are governed by quotient over multipliers and say nothing about degree N/8
claims.assessment: Finite check of low power (ranks one and two, degrees two and three)

claims.summary: Claim G, the general claim of the dense-forms line: for a source with n^c first-level flats there are value axioms E (linear equations in the bits or term values Z_c = e_c, chosen from the source) such that the base with E has no PC refutation of degree B and modulo E every block has an old image of degree s certified by the base and E; literal switching (Conjecture L) and generic term values (Question H) are its extreme cases; the compact bit base is itself a system of avoidance axioms for the collision flats, of total density about n/2, below the generic covering threshold
claims.assessment: Formulation stated by a route review for compiled sources; open, not asserted; candidate counterexample for arbitrary sources: the union of a wide literal reader and the row-mixing twisted approximate-majority source (incompatible axioms); hardness part recorded only for structured E (labels confined to one flat, matching restrictions)

claims.summary: The approximate-majority source of `thm:universal-Boolean-source-map-obstruction` (cycle 149) has, for any fixed set of at most 0.3 v coordinates, a circuit of the recorded form every term of which meets the complement I; modulo E = {u_i = 0, i in I} all its blocks have constant images (factor t-1 once). In the original coordinates, or under one affine bijection applied to every label, take the same 0.3 l bit positions in every row: the base with E is the compact base with n+1 rows and n^0.3 holes, hard through n^0.3/2 by `lem:compact-bit-ordinary-PC-decoder` and `cor:functional-auxiliary-PC-bridge`, so the recorded obstruction source satisfies Claim G. Under a generic row-mixing affine twist (p = 2, same barrier) it does exactly if the compact base has no low-degree refutation on a generic affine subspace of codimension about 0.7 v; this cannot be moved to the residual board
claims.assessment: Working reduction; original coordinates and row-by-row twists settled with recorded hardness, the row-mixing case open

claims.summary: Corollary SL: if a linear system over F_2 in the label bits is safe of rank a (one pivot in each of a distinct rows; Efremenko-Garlik-Itsykson) with 4(a-1) < n, every PC refutation of the functional unary base with the decoded system adjoined, hence of the compact base with the system, has degree at least n/2 - a + 1, for every right-hand side; corollary of `lem:top-row-linear-monomial-detector` by weighted replay with the indicator of the solution space (derivation due to the reviewer); a direct unary restriction leaves the functional PHP with n+1-a rows and n-2a holes; several pivots per row: `lem:multi-axis-cube-residual-detector` gives (n-F)/2 - (a-u) + 1; a uniformly random system of a <= n/4 equations is safe except with probability a 2^{-(m-a+1)l}; loss per equation equals the recorded case split
claims.assessment: Working proof (corollary of a recorded detector); does not reach rank above the number of blocks

claims.summary: Conjecture H1: for a uniformly random affine subspace W of the bit space the functional unary base with the decoded equations of W has PC refutation degree at least c min(n, dim W / l); elementary upper bound ceil(dim W / l) + O(1) in unary degree (projection to r rows with r l >= dim W + t is injective except with probability 2^-t); data: v - a* at tipping is 6 (eight holes) and 7 (sixteen holes) at degree two and 12 at degree three on eight holes, which does not decide the scaling, and the bijective control tips at the same free dimension at degree two
claims.assessment: Conjecture with three data points of low power; needed at dim W = 0.3 v for the row-mixing twist of `obs:twisted-approximate-majority-values`

claims.summary: Imported context: Miksa-Nordstrom Theorem 4.9 (graph functional PHP over an (s, delta)-boundary expander of left degree d needs PC degree > delta s/(2d)) would give at most n/(2d) for value axioms confining each row to its own flat if the flat graph expands (unchecked), transfer from the bit encoding not written out; Byramji-Impagliazzo (after Efremenko-Garlik-Itsykson): safe systems and closure for linear systems on the bit PHP, estimates for rank r <= cn; general Res(parity) described as open beyond depth N^(2-eps)
claims.assessment: Imported statements (arXiv versions, proofs not read)

claims.summary: Lemma R: over F_2, for independent consistent affine equations Lambda in the label bits with zero flat W and any injective affine parametrization P of W, the PC refutation bit degree of the compact base with Lambda equals max(l, degree of the collision-flat system {E_ii' o P} in the residual coordinates); the PHP on W is the statement that the collision flats of n+1 affine maps cover F_2^(dim W)
claims.assessment: Working proof, a composition of `lem:affine-coordinate-completion`, the substitution replay and the Boolean certificate of affine forms; Nullstellensatz dual (odd set meeting subflats evenly) recorded as a remark

claims.summary: Exact PC closures in residual coordinates for uniform subspaces (three seeds): largest refuted dimension at bit degree d is 9, 12, 16 on sixteen holes (d = 4, 5, 6) and 11, 15 on thirty-two (d = 5, 6), equal to the generic dimension count or one to two below it, with the bijective control within one; on eight holes 7 and 10 to 11 at d = 3, 4, and every subspace at d = 5 because the full base has bit degree exactly five (four holes: three)
claims.assessment: Finite check; it does not test Conjecture H1, whose bit form is implied by the trivial bound l for dim W <= 2 l^2 (only dim W <= 17 was reached, where the control is also unsatisfiable); it tests the stronger hypothesis that the degree stays within two of the generic count; tool research/tools/subspace_flat_cover_closure.cpp

claims.summary: A nonzero weight vanishing outside a subspace of codimension a has bit degree at least a, hence unary degree at least a/l, above the base barrier at codimension 0.7 v; a uniform subspace of codimension a contains no two points differing in at most r rows except with probability C(n+1,r) 2^(r l - a), hence no product of label sets with two points, so the recorded tensor-product designs (signed cubes, row trades) have no support inside it, while the affine restriction behind Corollary SL reserves two holes per equation
claims.assessment: Working observations from the failed proof attempt at Conjecture H1; weights with f Lambda_c in the old ideal only through the working degree are not excluded; Conjecture H1 parked untested next to Conjecture L

claims.summary: Lemma T: over F_2, a parity decision tree of depth d >= l for the collision search on an affine subspace W gives a Nullstellensatz certificate, hence a PC refutation, of the collision-flat system of bit degree at most d; D_b(W) <= max(l, depth) and <= max(l, dim W)
claims.assessment: Working proof; sharpens the l + d obtained from `lem:term-value-case-split`; uses only that the axioms are flat indicators

claims.summary: The compact bit base has PC bit degree between n/2+1 (recorded) and 2n-2+l (halving decision tree), and every affine subspace W has D_b(W) <= min(max(l, dim W), 2n-2+l); exact values 3 and 5 on four and eight holes
claims.assessment: Working corollary of Lemma T; settles order n against order n l

claims.summary: Corollary U: for a uniform affine subspace W of codimension a >= (N+1) l + log2 C(n+1,N+1) + t, except with probability 2^(-t) every restriction of the compact family leaves at most one point of W; on the union source the restriction for the literal reader and the generic equations for the twisted source cannot be combined
claims.assessment: Working corollary of `obs:subspace-design-attempt-obstructions`; Claim G itself is not refuted

claims.summary: Route review: the value method's hardness inputs, the union source and the unary parities of the simplest recorded unexcluded class (one OR over parities of PHP variables at middle rank) all need PHP hardness under linear constraints of rank of order v, while recorded and published techniques stop at rank of order n; the extension-variable methods of Dahiya-Mahajan-Mouli and Impagliazzo-Mouli-Pitassi need unnested definitions, (M + mn) kappa k = o(n^2), a formula surviving weight-pk assignments and the loss of kappa holes per round, an XOR lift, and p > 2
claims.assessment: Review with imported context; estimate for the value-method line about 5 percent; selects the parity-decision-tree depth on a generic subspace for at most two entries

claims.summary: Lemma L: for a uniform affine subspace W of dimension k, r l + log2 C(n+1,r) + t <= k (then r-2 <= n-1), except with probability 2^(-t) every parity decision tree solving the collision search on W has a path whose queries, in every representation, jointly touch more than r-2 rows; hence depth > (r-2)/omega for queries of row width omega, order n for ordinary decision trees at codimension 0.7 v
claims.assessment: Working proof (first moment on forms constant on W, onto projections to r rows, injective-point delayer); vacuous for l <= 4; supplies the proof of the free-rows sentence of #parity-subspace-remaining

claims.summary: Lemma D: if a parity decision tree of depth d solves the collision search on W, then for every nonempty G in W some affine subspace U of W inside a collision flat, of codimension s <= d, has |U cap G| >= 2^(-s) |G|; with G the points of image size n+1-j the prover needs a density boost (n+1)/(2 cbar_j) of near-injective labelings on an affine subspace of the flat
claims.assessment: Working proof; the delayer keeps the side with more of G

claims.summary: Exact Walsh spectra on four and eight holes: bijections have coefficient 1 on the n-1 uniform characters (all labels sum to zero), so boost n at codimension l; image size n-1 has largest coefficient 1/(n-1) (closed form on the uniform characters, maximal on four and eight holes); on eight holes no subspace of codimension <= 3 reaches the needed boost 2.0625, hence parity-decision-tree depth >= 7 for the full bit PHP on eight holes
claims.assessment: Finite check with two closed forms; the general spectral bound is logarithmic if the largest coefficient is 1/(n-1) for every n (unproved); ceiling: the birthday subspace (distinct prefixes on about sqrt(2 n ln(n/4)) rows) reaches the needed boost at codimension O(l sqrt(n log n)), so the density delayer with image size n-1 cannot prove more; Question A and the transfer to a generic subspace open

claims.summary: Lemma N: for an affine subspace H whose forms touch tau rows, revealing those rows in any order, the density boost of injective labelings on H is at most the product over pivot positions i of n/(n-i+1), at most n^tau (n-tau)!/n!, with equality on the birthday subspace (and on the sum-zero subspace); for labelings with exactly one colliding pair the same with n+3 (the proof gives n+2) in place of n
claims.assessment: Working proof; brute-force check on four and eight holes (no violation in 2400 random subspaces; attained for bijections; no power for the constant of the one-collision case, which rests on its proof); gives no depth bound beyond Lemma L and nothing for forms of large row width

claims.summary: Outcome of the two-entry parity-tree step: no strategy for unrestricted parity queries; absolute-value spectral arguments cannot pass codimension l sqrt(n/2) (heuristically about l^(3/2)); a mixed programme would end near (l^2 n)^(1/3); the transfer would reduce to the same signed sums over characters of large row width (not carried out; only the one-character second moment of the coefficients of G on W is proved); the parity-tree line and the value method (Claim G) are parked
claims.assessment: Context and decision; heuristic parts are labelled in the entry

claims.summary: Lemma K: substituting constants for the coefficient rows of complete first-level blocks maps P_b to Q_b = prod_u (1 - lambda_{b,u}), lambda in the span of the block; hence no degree-D PC refutation of the blocks if F with the axioms g_{b,i} Q_b has none, and none of a source with pure readers above if F with the axioms Q_b has none; no substitution factor, any rank; the first part over any prime, the second over F_2
claims.assessment: Working proof (degree-zero substitution plus the recorded reduction); the hypothesis is Question H at rank h with total density M 2^(-h), stronger than the zero-value hypothesis of the recorded reduction

claims.summary: Over F_2 and N >= 2B-1, an old polynomial t of degree k with a degree-d PC derivation from the functional unary base plus M fresh blocks with old inputs of degree at most delta (any rank and accuracy) lies in I_k of the base when d + M max(delta, k) <= B; so M blocks give no refutation and no old consequence of degree k while d + M max(delta, k) <= (N+1)/2
claims.assessment: Working corollary of lem:old-consequence-transfer and the stable filtration; additive in M, nothing for M >= N/2

claims.summary: For the recorded approximate-majority parameters every hitting set of the terms has density above 0.47 with high probability, so every point allowed by the term values Z_c = 0 lies on a coordinate subspace of codimension above 0.47 v; term values move the Conjecture H1 instance from dimension 0.3 v to at most about 0.53 v
claims.assessment: Working count (union bound over sets of size 0.47 v); the 'exactly if' of the earlier test holds for its linear E only

claims.summary: Route review: every form with a recorded polynomial-calculus exclusion at a degree not tied to the accuracy is a design of an enlarged old base composed with old images, needing hardness H(E); forms outside the type (source-module moment designs, fresh-block conservativity, proof-specific forms) with their recorded status; table of what each method pays for M blocks of window rank in the one-level unary family; statement (HW): the unary base with M <= N^c generic avoidance axioms of width h, M 2^(-h) < 1, has no PC refutation of polylogarithmic degree; selected for at most two entries at the NS level
claims.assessment: Review; (HW) open; no finite evidence in its regime (the recorded closures at larger density show no early failure in the counting regime)

claims.summary: Lemma E: for the functional unary base over F_2 in matching normal form with clauses Q_b of degree h and G_e = I_e + sum_b Q_b P_{<=e-h}: if G_B cap P_{<=B-1} = G_{B-1} the normal-form PC closure at degree B is G_B; if this holds at every level 1..B then 1 is not in G_B and there is no PC refutation of degree B; no relation between N and B is used
claims.assessment: Working proof; the general one-level form of the recorded truncated-closure induction (stable filtration, transported and conditioned bit classes)

claims.summary: Observation F: for X in Y in P_{<=e}, dim X - dim(X cap P_{<=e-1}) <= dim top_e(Y); so a fall at level e is forced once dim G_e - dim G_{e-1} > m_e, and for forms in a space L once the multiples with multipliers from L exceed the top-degree part of I_{h+1} + L^{h+1}
claims.assessment: Working proof (rank of the top-degree projection); explains the recorded closure jumps

claims.summary: Exact NS spaces over F_2 of the functional unary base with random clauses of h parities (six holes B=3 h=2; seven holes B=4 h=2,3; eight holes B=3 h=2 with general and with decoded bit-affine forms): dim G_B increments c_1-h and c_2-2c_1+3-(b-1) for every clause, 1 enters only at exhaustion (general forms) or at exhaustion of the cubic part of the subalgebra of the forms (label forms, clause 126), first fall exactly at the forced clause (50; 23; 351; 264; label forms 91 with excess 7 = 25*91-2268), except a fall of one at slack 0 or 1 in four of six boundary events; label parity constraints fall first at clauses 19, 19, 20 (degree two; forced at 20, slack one at 19) and 15 (degree three); the recorded PC jumps (50, 91; general parity constraints 15, 32, 17; label parity constraints 19, 19, 20 and 15) are these falls
claims.assessment: Finite check; seeds give identical generic ranks; degrees two to four, h <= 3

claims.summary: Conjecture SR: for uniform forms from a space L (all affine forms, or unary images of bit-affine forms) dim G_B follows H_R(t)(1 - t^h/(1+t)^h)^M, no degree fall occurs before the first clause at which the forced-fall count holds for a pair X = I_e + sum_b Q_b L^d, Y = I_e + L^(d+h) (unary degrees), up to O(1) clauses, and 1 enters only when I_B + L^B lies in G_B; with Lemma E this would give (HW) for generic clauses up to about gamma_B/gamma_{B-h} clauses (order (N^2/B)^h; for label forms a heuristic upper estimate ((N+1)log N/B)^h)
claims.assessment: Conjecture with finite evidence only (degrees two to four, h <= 3); stronger than what (HW) needs; no proof technique on record

claims.summary: In (HW) the codimension of a clause is counted modulo the row sums: the sum of all column sums is constant modulo I_1, so a parity tree that queries it first gives 2^(h-1) clauses of nominal codimension h summing to 1 at degree h; the N onto axioms 1+kappa_j give a degree-one NS refutation over F_2 (classical). A shortcut fails: replacing satisfiable clauses by linear equations at a satisfying value of the forms needs hardness at a chosen right-hand side, which the record has only for safe bit-linear systems (Corollary SL); 1+x_11, 1+x_21 is a counterexample
claims.assessment: Working remarks (falsification attempts of the entry; the failed shortcut found by the reviewer)

claims.summary: Theorem T2: for the functional unary base over F_2 (N >= 3) with parity constraints a_b = l_b + c_b whose linear parts are independent modulo the row sums, if no nonzero element of Kbar (image in Lambda^2 V of the span of products of conflicting cells, dim (N+1)(2N^2-3N+2)/2) vanishes on the annihilator U of the forms, then G_2 cap P_{<=1} = G_1, 1 is not in the degree-two closure, and there is no PC refutation of degree two; fails for one-row forms, column sums (the recorded occupancy equations), and is forced to fail when C(d,2) < dim Kbar
claims.assessment: Working proof (top coefficients, Cartan's lemma, idempotence, stability at B = 2); sufficient, not necessary; arbitrary-multiplier analogue of the recorded quadratic-faithfulness tests

claims.summary: Over F_2: a form of rank 2 rho vanishes on a uniform d-subspace with probability at most 2.39 * 2^(rho(rho+1)/2 - rho d) (Lagrangian count), and at most 6 * 2^((log2 d)^2/6 - C(d,2)) when rho >= d (sequential exposure); Kbar has at most C(n, 2 rho) 2^(2 rho (3N-2)) elements of rank 2 rho (a symmetric matrix of rank r is determined by r rows spanning its row space; each row of a conflict form has at most 2^(3N-2) possibilities)
claims.assessment: Working proofs

claims.summary: Theorem U: for M independent uniform affine forms and d = N^2-1-M with C(d,2) >= dim Kbar + (log2 d)^2/6 + s and d >= 12N + 8 log2 N + 2s, with probability at least 1 - 2^(-d) - 7*2^(-s) the base with the parity constraints has no degree fall at levels one and two and no PC refutation of degree two; asymptotically M <= N^2 - sqrt2 N^(3/2) (1+o(1)), matching the forced count
claims.assessment: Working proof (first moment over Kbar by rank); degree two only, uniform forms only, asymptotic (N above about 80)

claims.summary: Theorem Lb with its structure lemma: for N = 2^l >= 16, Kbar cap (Lbar wedge V) is the direct sum over rows of Lbar_i wedge V_i (on eight holes the constant cross terms remain: 171 = 135 + 36); hence for M uniform decoded bit-affine parity constraints, d_L = (N+1) l - M with C(d_L,2) >= (N+1) C(l,2) + (log2 d_L)^2/6 + s and d_L >= l^2 + l + 4 + 2s, no degree fall and no PC refutation of unary degree two with probability at least 1 - N^2 2^(-d_L) - 9*2^(-s): a uniform affine subspace of the bit space of dimension above about l sqrt(N+1), which includes the case dim W = 0.3 v of Conjecture H1, at degree two only; not sharp for refutations (recorded tipping at dim W = 6, 7) and silent on bit degree
claims.assessment: Working proof; structure lemma checked numerically on sixteen holes (850)

claims.summary: 3750 random instances on four, six, eight and sixteen holes (uniform and label forms): the criterion of Theorem T2 never holds together with a degree fall; on six, eight and sixteen holes it fails exactly in the instances with a fall, on four holes also without a fall (2 to 23 of 200 per M); falls from the forced count in every instance (sixteen holes, label forms: none for M <= 53, all for M >= 54); falls before the forced count on small boards are the low-rank events of the first moment; exact enumeration confirms Lemmas R1, R2 in 40 small cases
claims.assessment: Finite check of Theorem T2 only; Theorems U and Lb are asymptotic and rest on their proofs

claims.summary: Decision after the two entries on (HW): evidence and a degree-two proof that generic wide forms do no harm before a count forces it, by a method whose cost is not additive in the number of forms; at degree three and above a fall is an element of the conflict ideal that vanishes on U outside Wbar wedge Kbar_{B-1}, the event "vanishes on U" is dominated by the trivial one (for decomposable elements the two coincide under the criterion), and a first moment needs a rank of B-forms relative to the ideal with a count of low-rank elements, which is not known; (HW) parked next to Question H; next: review of the forms outside the type
claims.assessment: Decision; the degree-B form of the statement is not proved

claims.summary: A degree-D complete affine ENS refutation forces dim(U intersect old-PC-k(D+1)) at least dim(U) minus the summed proper-high-flat restriction dimensions
claims.assessment: Lean-verified in full over F_2 for arbitrary finite variables, old base, accuracy and subspace, with the nonzero-consequence, exclusion, uniform-threshold and empty-index corollaries; the CNF initial-value bridge remark is not covered; not a general PC-refutation degree bound
